detail:
MedlinePlus describes blood pressure as the force of blood pushing against the walls of the arteries, recorded as two numbers: systolic pressure, when the heart beats, over diastolic pressure, when the heart rests between beats. High blood pressure, also called hypertension, is the condition in which that force stays at levels clinicians consider high over time. MedlinePlus notes it usually has no symptoms, so regular blood pressure checks are described as the only way a person learns the levels are high.

MedlinePlus distinguishes primary, or essential, hypertension, the most common type, which usually develops over time with age, from secondary hypertension, which is caused by another medical condition or by certain medicines. Sources link sustained high blood pressure to the heart working harder over time and to higher risk of heart attack, stroke, heart failure, and kidney failure. Diagnosis in the sources rests on repeated blood pressure readings taken by a health care provider rather than on symptoms.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about high blood pressure and how it is monitored.
summary: MedlinePlus explains blood pressure as the force of blood against artery walls, describes hypertension as pressure that stays at levels clinicians consider high, and notes it usually causes no symptoms and is found through regular checks.
takeaways: high blood pressure usually causes no symptoms, sources describe
primary hypertension is the most common type and develops over time
repeated readings, not symptoms, are how it is found
title: Hypertension: high blood pressure with no symptoms
